claims.explanation: TWS-119 is a GSK3 inhibitor, and its selective killing likely reflects dependence on GSK3-driven survival and Wnt/β-catenin signaling, with additional contribution from its reported activities against JUN/MYC-related transcriptional programs. Lines with high GSK3B expression, active Wnt/β-catenin signaling, or MYC/JUN-driven transcriptional addiction are predicted to be most sensitive, while low GSK3B or low Wnt activity would be protective.

features.basis: primary annotated target; higher target expression increases dependence on GSK3 activity
Wnt/β-catenin activation is modulated by GSK3 inhibition and predicts pathway dependence
annotated target and virtual-cell MYC downregulation suggests MYC-addicted lines are more affected
annotated target; AP-1/JUN-driven lines may depend on GSK3-modulated JUN activity
virtual cell shows CCND1 downregulation, linking GSK3 inhibition to cell-cycle arrest in cyclin-D1-high lines
APC loss activates Wnt independently of GSK3, reducing dependence on GSK3 inhibition
AXIN mutations can activate β-catenin downstream of GSK3, bypassing the drug's effect
p53 loss may allow survival despite GSK3 inhibition-induced stress
virtual cell shows MTHFD2 downregulation, suggesting one-carbon metabolism dependence
virtual cell shows SERPINE1 downregulation, a TGF-β/EMT-associated survival factor
virtual cell upregulation of FGFR2 suggests FGFR-dependent lines may be more responsive
transcriptional similarity to EGFR inhibitor canertinib suggests EGFR-pathway dependence
